page: Microsoft Azure DC64ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. System resources include 256.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The underlying x86_64 architecture provides advanced instruction extensions, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic accelerators, complemented by 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache.

Storage capabilities include a 2577 GB local SSD along with support for Azure Premium Storage. In benchmark testing, the AMD EPYC architecture exhibits strong processing output, registering a stress-ng single-core score of 3023.68 and a multi-core score of 96117.69, both placing within the top 25 percent of tested systems. Memory and cache handling demonstrate high throughput during database operations, logging 82.48 million operations per second on redis SET benchmarks.

The dense core and memory allotment yields solid qualitative cost efficiency for organizations consolidating multi-threaded enterprise services and data-heavy operations onto single nodes. Tradeoffs include the lack of discrete GPU accelerators, limiting its utility for deep learning training, and the absence of complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Microsoft Azure DC64ads_v6 is well suited for large database deployments, in-memory key-value stores, batch analytics, and high-concurrency application servers requiring fast local scratch storage.

The configuration couples 256.0 GB of system memory at a balanced 4.0 GB per core with 2577 GB of integrated local SSD storage, alongside Azure Premium Storage capability. The x86_64 CPU incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, as well as hardware-level cryptographic acceleration. In standard benchmarks, DC64ads_v6 delivers strong performance, achieving top-quartile results in stress-ng multi-core tests with 96117.69 and single-core tests with 3023.68. Memory pipeline efficiency is evidenced by a throughput of 82.48 million operations per second in redis SET benchmarks. Lacking discrete GPUs and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance is targeted at compute-heavy enterprise backends, high-throughput in-memory caching systems, distributed relational databases, and microservice clusters requiring high local storage capacity.
